root_cause.text: The USB device reference obtained via usb_get_dev() in create_card() is not released on probe failure because the card_free() destructor (which calls usb_put_dev()) is assigned to ->private_free too late (only at the end of init_card()), so if any intermediate operation fails, snd_card_free() is called without the destructor set, leaving the reference leaked.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly states: "->private_free is only assigned near the end of init_card(), after several failure points... When any of those fail, ... ->private_free is still NULL, card_free() never runs, the usb_get_dev() reference is not dropped, and the struct usb_device leaks." The patch moves the assignment into create_card() immediately after usb_get_dev().

    ALSA: caiaq: Use snd_card_free_when_closed() at disconnection
    
    The USB disconnect callback is supposed to be short and not too-long
    waiting.  OTOH, the current code uses snd_card_free() at

    can take long.  It eventually blocks the upper layer USB ioctls, which

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit adds a `card_free` destructor but assigns it via `card->private_free = card_free` only at the end of `init_card()`, after `setup_card()` and before `return 0`. If an error occurs earlier in `init_card()` (e.g., at `err_kill_urb`), the destructor is not set, so a failure before that point will not release the USB reference obtained via `usb_get_dev()` in `create_card()`. This matches the root cause: the destructor is assigned too late, leaving the reference leaked on probe failure. The change to `snd_disconnect()` is unrelated to this vulnerability.
